newsitem.title: UK: EU sugar beets need moisture to avoid harvest dela.
newsitem.headline: EU sugar beets need moisture to avoid harvest dela.

text.p: European Union (EU) sugar beets are still vulnerable to dry weather and the 1997/98 harvest could be delayed if low moisture levels do not improve, Czarnikow Sugar said in a report on Thursday.
"The crop has made good progress and is well placed to capitalise on further good weather, if it arrives," the report said.
"But the plants are still more than usually vulnerable to further periods of dry weather as sub-soil moisture levels remain exceedingly low," it said.
Czarnikow said the early sown crops could well achieve full leaf coverage as early as possible so they could then maximise their capability to generate sugar.

It noted that more rain was needed in France, the EU's largest producer, where irrigation restrictions were still in force. Dry conditions had also been reported in southern Germany and south east Europe.
"Any worsening of the (moisture) situation could well delay the start of the harvest, thereby aggravating an already tight supply situation this summer," it said.
